channel.title: Wire — AI
channel.description: AI from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash-1017
item.description: We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Show HN: Gemini 4 Argon plays StarCraft
item.description: StarSkirmish: where LLMs write code to play StarCraft. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Reverse Engineer Anything Project Brings AI Agents to Binary Analysis
item.description: Reverse Engineer Anything (REA) is an open-source project with over 200K GitHub stars that connects coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex to reverse-engineering tools like Ghidra, Hopper, and IDA. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Postgres 19 delayed after AI reviewers find more bugs than humans can fix
item.description: Core devs revert up to 10 features, push release to November, and blame better tooling rather than vibe coding (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Do you let LLMs write both your tests and your code?
item.description: I'm curious what stance others have taken? Or what they've experienced with this? I'm toying with adding a rule to our values.md that the LLM can only significantly generate one or the other. (1 source: lobsters)

item.title: AI in Production: Panellists Highlight Silent Failures, Harness Engineering, and Agent Governance
item.description: A recent InfoQ webinar examined operational challenges in deploying agentic systems. Key points included issues like semantic and embedding drift, which can lead to significant errors. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: 90% of US working hours are spent on tasks not covered well by AI benchmarks
item.description: The US Benchmark Map places AI benchmarks across the American economy, measuring which parts of the labor force are covered by unsaturated, public, agentic benchmarks. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Anthropic assigned highest junk credit rating in June
Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins
item.description: The decades-old mystery of the origins of one of the most popular cryptographic standards has been explained. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: The Decoherence Trap: When AI slop drowns out the signal in an endless sea of noise
item.description: Of all the forms of tech debt, decoherence is the worst. It compounds exponentially with a system's rate of change, and AI is now producing it faster than ever, leading us deeper and deeper into the abyss... (1 source: lobsters)
